Definition: middle voice from G303 and G906; to put off (for oneself):--defer.
BiblicalUsage: The word appears once: Felix, having more perfect knowledge of the Way, deferred Paul's case and said, 'When Lysias the chief captain shall come down, I will know the uttermost of your matter.' It is a putting off — the governor knew enough to decide and chose to wait instead, and Paul stayed in prison two more years.
TheologicalSignificance: One word for putting off carries no doctrine of its own; its weight is Felix's delay — a man who knew the truth and kept putting the decision off until it was too late.
RelatedEvents: Paul Before Felix, Festus, and Agrippa
